claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The narrative refers to 'the fact that Jessica had been diagnosed as near-sighted,' which describes a medical circumstance rather than an out-of-court assertion by a declarant.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as an out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted. Non-assertive facts or circumstances do not qualify as hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: the fact that Jessica had been diagnosed as near-sighted by her ophthalmologist.

arguments.text: The evidence is introduced 'on the issue of whether Jessica was aware she was trespassing,' indicating it is offered to prove her state of mind or circumstantial awareness rather than the truth of an asserted proposition.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires evidence be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted. Evidence offered for another purpose, such as proving a party's state of mind or circumstantial awareness, falls outside the hearsay definition.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Jessica was aware she was trespassing
